sections.label: Statutory Boards and legislation
sections.summary: Legislation must reflect intent and balance, and Singapore now has 61 Statutory Boards listed in the Bill's Schedule.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Legislation must reflect that intent and that balance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: There are now 61 Statutory Boards in Singapore delivering services in respective areas listed in the Schedule of the Bill.

sections.label: Bill objectives for Statutory Boards
sections.summary: The Bill aims to standardise governance requirements, make corporate policy compliance explicit, improve data-sharing, and amends five Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The central agencies, which are the Public Service Division and the Ministry of Finance (MOF), together with Smart Nation and Digital Government Office and the Ministry of Communications and Information, recently did a comprehensive stocktake of all these Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This Bill will reduce and minimise this unevenness, with a view to institutionalise a clearer and more consistent governance framework for Statutory Boards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It will, therefore, achieve three main objectives: first, standardise key governance requirements amongst Statutory Boards; second, make explicit requirements for Statutory Boards to comply with key corporate policies in human resource (HR), finance, office administration and information technology (IT), and they are already doing so by abiding the Government Instruction Manual (IM), but we should provide for formal legislative backing; third, improve the data-sharing scheme, and I am specifically addressing this governance policy because it is a more recent requirement; and finally, this Bill also makes related amendments to five Acts.

sections.label: Appointment and removal of CEs
sections.summary: The Bill standardises the Minister's role in approving appointment and removal of CEs, subject to PSC concurrence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill also standardises the role of the Minister to approve the appointment and removal of CEs, subject to the concurrence of the Public Service Commission (PSC).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, it is a three-key system – the Board of Directors of the Statutory Board appoint the CE, the Minister approves, and PSC concurs.

sections.label: Minister directions to Statutory Boards
sections.summary: The Bill empowers the Minister for the Singapore public sector to issue directions to Statutory Boards on central policies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill empowers the Minister charged with the responsibility for the Singapore public sector to issue directions to Statutory Boards to comply with those central policies, jointly with the Minister responsible for the respective policy areas.

sections.label: Purposes of central directions
sections.summary: The Bill limits central directions to seven purposes, including public sector values, economies, efficiency, business continuity, stewardship, risk and whole-of-Government approach.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To guide the setting of central policy directives, the Bill stipulates that the relevant Ministers are only empowered to give central directions for the following purposes: (a) upholding and promoting the values of the Singapore public sector; (b) securing economies or efficiencies for the Singapore public sector; (c) improving the efficiency or effectiveness of policies and programmes; (d) ensuring business continuity in case of emergencies; (e) ensuring accountable and prudent stewardship of Singapore public sector finances and resources; (f) managing risks to the financial position of the Government; and (g) finally, supporting a whole-of-Government approach in the discharge of the Statutory Boards' functions.

sections.label: Formalising data-sharing regime
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to formalise the data-sharing regime within the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The third area that this Bill seeks to achieve is to formalise the data-sharing regime within the Public Service.

sections.label: Public sector data sharing purposes
sections.summary: The Bill provides bases for data sharing between public sector agencies, with seven public interest purposes under the Minister's direction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: First, the Bill provides the bases for data to be shared between public sector agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Specifically, there are seven purposes supporting public interest, under which data can be shared under the direction of the Minister.

sections.label: Accountability for shared data
sections.summary: The Bill makes the user of shared data accountable for its protection and safeguarding, correcting the current asymmetry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The requesting agency is using the data, but yet the owner is responsible and accountable for the security of the data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This Bill will correct this asymmetry and make it clear that it is the user who will be accountable for the protection and safeguarding of data passed to them.

sections.label: People's Association treatment amendments
sections.summary: Amendments will be moved at Committee stage to bring the treatment of the People's Association in line with similar Statutory Boards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Related to this, I will later move amendments at the Committee stage to bring the treatment of People's Association (PA) more in line with that of similar Statutory Boards.

sections.label: Fire Safety and Police Force amendments
sections.summary: Amendments to the Fire Safety Act and Police Force Act remove references to the divisional status of public officers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Two, amendments to the Fire Safety Act and Police Force Act to remove references to the divisional status of public officers.

sections.label: Government Contracts Act amendment
sections.summary: An amendment to the Government Contracts Act allows seconded Statutory Board employees to execute binding contracts on behalf of Government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Three, an amendment to the Government Contracts Act to allow Statutory Board employees on secondment to the Government to execute binding contracts on behalf of Government.

sections.label: PSC and LSC Act alignment
sections.summary: The PSC and LSC Act is amended to remove the phrase "acting in his discretion" from two sections, aligning it with the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Article 21 of the Constitution states that the President must, in exercising her statutory functions, act in accordance with the advice of the Cabinet, except as provided by the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: However, the text of two sections of the PSC and LSC Act is inconsistent with this because it states that the President can exercise her discretion to permit the communication, publication and disclosure of information relating to the Commissions' work, which should not otherwise be disclosed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Article 162 of the Constitution requires any law pre-dating the Constitution to be brought into alignment with the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, we are taking this opportunity to amend the PSC and LSC Act to remove the phrase "acting in his discretion" from two sections of the Act.

sections.label: Public benefits from Government data
sections.summary: The speaker expects public support if benefits are visible and hopes implementation prioritises areas with significant social impact for low-income, seniors and the under-privileged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Thus, I am sure that the public will welcome this move if they can see the direct benefits that it brings them in transacting with the Government and in how they use various Government services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I hope that with the implementation of this Bill, the Government will prioritise to start with areas that can have significant social impact, especially those for the low-income, seniors and the under-privileged.

sections.label: Data access for assistance schemes
sections.summary: The speaker asks that officers handling welfare, housing and health subsidies get greater data access and suggests a points-based eligibility system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: An example involves Government assistance schemes that need salary declarations to determine household income, but the Government may already have had some salary information either through income tax declarations or CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I ask that officers handling such sensitive cases for welfare, housing and health subsidies be given greater access to data to make decisions more easily and, more importantly, to reduce the burden on the residents to keep providing updated statements and data every few months when assistance needs to be renewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Government work on a points-based system to determine the eligibility of citizens for various schemes, similar to what we do for credit scoring?

sections.label: Business administrative filing burden
sections.summary: The speaker says companies' time and resources on administrative filings can be drastically reduced through data sharing among Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: From the business point of view, for example, the amount of time and resources companies spend in administrative filings, whether for taxes, specific permits and licences or manpower quotas, can be drastically reduced through the sharing of data among Government agencies.

sections.label: Assurance against citizen tracking
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Government plans to assure citizens that they are not actively being tracked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How does the Government plan to assure citizens that they are not actively being tracked?

sections.label: Data accuracy, declarations and penalties
sections.summary: The speaker asks how citizens and businesses can check and self-update data, whether officers must declare interests and holdings, and whether stronger penalties will be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With this Bill, an outdated or erroneous data is now transmitted across multiple agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: So, how can a citizen or a business find out whether the data that the Government has on them is actually correct and if they can self-update easily, without the hassle of checking from agency to agency?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will there be measures put in place for such officers to declare interests beyond the grade ones that the Minister shared earlier, and holdings of investment and properties?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Government also consider stronger penalties for breaches of data access or leaks so as to create stronger deterrents?

sections.label: Bill's governance framework purpose
sections.summary: The long title states the Bill seeks a consistent governance framework across public bodies and supports a whole-of-Government approach to service delivery.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the long title of the Bill, it seeks to provide for a consistent governance framework across the public bodies and to support the whole-of-Government approach to the delivery of services.

sections.label: Accountability between Ministers and agencies
sections.summary: Part 2 sets out the accountability relationships between Government Ministers and public sector agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More critically, Part 2 prescribes the accountability relationships between Government Ministers and the public sector agencies.

sections.label: Statutory Boards listed in Schedule
sections.summary: The Bill's Schedule lists 50 Statutory Boards in Groups 1A and 1B, including ACRA, CPF Board, HDB, LTA and PUB.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Statutory Boards in question are listed in the Schedule to the Bill under Group 1A and Group 1B of the First Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These bodies total 50 in number and include major public functions that affect the lives of Singaporeans across the board, for example, the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority, Central Provident Fund Board, Housing and Development Board, Land Transport Authority and Public Utilities Board.

sections.label: Ministerial direction not binding
sections.summary: A Ministerial direction is not binding if it would impede a statutorily independent or quasi-judicial function of a public sector agency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A Ministerial direction is also not binding if it would impede or affect the performance of a statutorily independent function of a public sector agency or a quasi-judicial function of a public sector agency in a particular matter.

sections.label: Clause widely worded, no definition
sections.summary: The clause is very widely worded because it does not define what sorts of acts are contemplated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, the clause is very widely worded as there is no definition of what sorts of acts are contemplated.

sections.label: Clause 11 and public sector agencies
sections.summary: Clause 11 bars Ministers from issuing offending directions to public sector agencies as defined in clause 2.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 11 says that Ministers cannot issue the offending directions to public sector agencies, which are defined in clause 2 to mean Statutory Boards listed in Groups 1, 2 and 3 of the Schedule, a Ministry or department of Government, an Organ of State, or a public officer or person as gazetted by the Minister.

sections.label: Restrictions easy to circumvent
sections.summary: The restrictions on Ministerial directions appear easy to circumvent, for example by a Minister speaking to a public officer on the side.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, Sir, while these restrictions on Ministerial directions are impressive on paper, they appear to me easy to circumvent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, what is there to stop a Minister from speaking to a public officer on the side to get such things done, thus bypassing the prohibitions in clause 11?

sections.label: Minister directives to share data
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Minister direct sector agencies to share information with another sector agency to improve public sector efficiency or effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, the Minister may give sector agencies directives to share information under the control of the sector agency with another sector agency to improve, whether directly or indirectly, the efficiency or effectiveness of policies, programme management or service planning and delivery by public sector agencies, whether by carrying out data analytics work or otherwise.

sections.label: Data sharing and PDPA exemption
sections.summary: The Bill covers sharing and re-identification of anonymised information, and asks whether guidelines secure data handling given the public sector's PDPA exemption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, under the Bill, data sharing includes the sharing of information or re-identification of anonymised information under the control of the sector agency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Third, are there guidelines in place to ensure that the collection, transfer and handling of data are secure, bearing in mind that the public sector is exempted from the provisions of the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA)?

sections.label: Audit of automated processing
sections.summary: The passage asks what audit processes ensure automated processing of information and algorithms are soundly evaluated to minimise bias and error.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: What audit processes are in place to ensure that any automated processing of information and algorithms are soundly evaluated to minimise bias and error?

sections.label: Clause 11(3) ministerial limits
sections.summary: Clause 11(3) states Ministers cannot direct a public sector agency, public body or public officer to perform or not perform a particular act regarding particular persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Clause 11(3) states that Ministers are not authorised to direct any public sector agency or any public body or public officer to perform or not to perform a particular act with respect to a particular person or persons.

sections.label: Public servants moving to politics
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore public servants have moved into politics immediately after leaving the Public Service, joining the ruling Party as MPs or Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, we have a history of public servants moving on to take up roles in politics immediately upon leaving the Public Service, primarily by joining the ruling Party and serving as MPs or Ministers in the PAP Government with little or no break in between.

sections.label: MAS cooling-off period confirmed
sections.summary: In the Banking Act debate, Minister Ong Ye Kung confirmed a mandatory time gap existed for MAS officers resigning to join financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the debate on the Banking Act, I had asked then, coincidentally Minister Ong Ye Kung as well, if such a mandatory time gap, referred to in that context as "garden leave" or a cooling-off period, existed for Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) officers who wished to resign from MAS and join the financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: He confirmed that such a mandatory time gap existed.

sections.label: Mandatory time gap for public servants
sections.summary: A mandatory three-year gap before public servants join politics would deter partisan bidding to win ruling Party favour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Imposing a mandatory time gap between when one can leave the Public Service and when one can join politics, say, three years, would give pause to any ambitious public servant who might seek to read their political masters' mind and do their partisan bidding unasked, so as to facilitate their chances of joining the ruling Party as an elected politician.

sections.label: Benefits of mandatory time gap
sections.summary: A mandatory time gap would give future MPs private sector experience, alternative employment and time to reflect on entering politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Such a rule would also have other benefits than the one I have mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It would ensure that future MPs and Ministers from the Civil Service would need to have private sector and/or not-for-profit sector experience prior to becoming MPs and Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore's first Cabinet, upon the attainment of self-government, the proportion of civil servants was far, far less than in the Cabinets that followed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And the period of time during the mandatory time gap would also allow them an alternative form of employment to give them the time and space to reflect if they really do want to enter politics, so that those who eventually do take that step may prove to be more committed to that pathway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I hope that some form of mandatory time gap can be considered for ex-public servants seeking to join politics.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But the spirit of the Bill was more ambitious though, particularly the use or development of IT, such as big data analytics, block-chain technology and artificial intelligence (AI).

sections.label: Statutory Boards compliance with directions
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Ministers are concerned that Statutory Boards may not have complied with directions.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Two, are Ministers concerned that there may be directions that have not been complied with by Statutory Boards?

sections.label: Bill silent on whistleblowers
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill appears silent on the important point of whistleblowers.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Nine, the Bill seems to be silent on an important point, which is about whistleblowers.

sections.label: Parliament role in public sector governance
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Parliament can play a role in public sector governance and identifying causes of hazards.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: KOM pays a large fine, Singapore pays an incalculably higher one.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In such instances, as far as public sector governance goes, could there be something that Parliament can do?

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I am not talking about the legal accountability, I am not talking about criminal procedure and justice, but is there a role for Parliament to play, perhaps within select committees or Parliamentary commissions, to look at situations that could guide Government-linked companies and Statutory Boards were there ever to be a situation where they would fear that someone should come forward to speak about a point or there is a danger of a serious wrongdoing?

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A critical issue, Mr Deputy Speaker, and let me end on this point, is to identify why a hazard occurred, what factors – environmental, organisational, human, cultural – were potential causative factors, and how the risk of a similar event occurring again can be reduced.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This requires patience to recognise that no system will be able to prevent every adverse event from occurring, that people should work together collaboratively to ensure this does not happen again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This Bill gives Government Ministers powers to direct all Singapore public sector agencies relating to certain matters so as to “uphold the values of the Singapore public sector.” This includes powers to give directions relating to the management of official records.

sections.label: Minister powers and NLB records powers
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Minister's proposed powers over official records would work with NLB's existing powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How would the proposed powers of the relevant Minister to direct public sector agencies or public bodies in the management of official records work in conjunction with the existing powers of the NLB relating to the retention and preservation of public records?

sections.label: Uniform public sector governance framework
sections.summary: The Bill aims to create a uniform governance framework across Singapore's public sector, with five points serving as broad guides.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I agree that these five points serve as broad guides for us.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This Bill, Sir, aims to create a uniform governance framework across the public sector in Singapore.

sections.label: Data sharing directives details
sections.summary: A Member asks for more details on section 6 of the Bill concerning data sharing directives.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In section 6 of the Bill, pertaining to the “data sharing directives”, can we have some more details on this?

sections.label: MUIS exemption and politicisation definition
sections.summary: A Member asks whether MUIS is exempted from clauses 34 to 41 and seeks the Minister's definition and examples of "politicised".

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Based on my understanding, clause 33 states that the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS), categorised in Group 3A Public Bodies, is exempted from clauses 34 to 41.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If it is correct, can the Minister provide the reasons for this exemption?

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My colleague, Ms Sylvia Lim, had earlier touched on that explanatory note stating that the introduction of clause 11 was "to ensure that the public sector, like the Singapore Public Service, not be politicised".

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It would be much appreciated if the Minister can define and elaborate more on the word "politicised" as stated in the explanatory note and also to cite an example or two so that Members will have a clearer and better understanding of the phrase "not be politicised".

sections.label: PA politicisation and data sharing
sections.summary: A Member asks whether PA is being politicised and notes constraints in sharing personal data between public bodies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As such, I seek the Minister's reply as to whether PA, a Statutory Board, which is a public service entity, is being politicised in the above-mentioned scenarios.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Although the PDPA does not apply to Government agencies, I understand that there have been constraints in the sharing of personal data between public bodies due to the Government’s own data policies.

sections.label: Clarifications on privacy and data consequences
sections.summary: A Member seeks clarifications on privacy, security, consent and consequences of failures such as re-identification and unauthorised access.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also wish to seek a few clarifications concerning privacy and confidentiality, security, non–discrimination, consent, transparency and accountability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand it is not possible to enumerate but it would be helpful if we could have some indications; (b) when disclosure could be authorised; (c) when the use of information would be considered proper; (d) the consequences of failing to ensure end-to-end encryption or failing to ensure anonymisation of data that should have been anonymised; (e) the consequences of re-identification of anonymised information by a former "relevant public official".

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The current provisions, as drafted, cover only abuse by current relevant public officials; and (f) the consequences of unauthorised access to data.

sections.label: Penalty for non-disclosure of conflict
sections.summary: A Member asks the Government's position on non-disclosure of a conflict of interest and why no specific penalty provision exists.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In relation to Part 4 of the Bill, given that non-disclosure of a conflict of interest is a serious matter, what is the position of the Government in this respect, and is there a particular reason why there is no specific provision to penalise non-disclosure?

sections.label: Bill long title and purposes
sections.summary: The passage quotes the Bill's long title and section 3 purposes, and notes the Bill does not require a whole-of-Government approach to services to the public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The long title of the Bill reads, "An Act to provide for a consistent governance framework across public bodies in Singapore and to support a whole-of-Government approach to the delivery of services in the Singapore public sector, and to make consequential and related amendments to certain other Acts." I am curious why the reference to a consistent governance framework in the long title refers only to public bodies and not to Singapore public service agencies as a whole.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also note that in section 3 of the Bill, the purposes of the Bill are stated as follows: (a) to establish a consistent system of governance and accountability across public bodies in Singapore that meets high standards of accountability; (b) to clarify the accountability relationship between public bodies, the members, the responsible Ministers and the Government; and (c) to require and support a whole-of-Government approach to the delivery of services in the Singapore public sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But if this piece of legislation is inadequately understood or executed, it will fall to be another set of compliance burden.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is noted that the Bill does not require and support a whole-of-Government approach to the delivery of services by the public sector to the public.

sections.label: Public service cardinal principles
sections.summary: The passage argues the Bill should enshrine two cardinal principles of public service, the first being that the public service exists to serve the public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It can potentially revolutionise the delivery of public sector services and shape the public sector to come.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would submit that it should at least enshrine two cardinal principles of public service.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The first cardinal principle, that is, the public service exists to serve the public, that principle must set the tone and context for the subsidiary legislation, policies, instruction manuals and the implementation to follow.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This cardinal principle will be a constant reminder to public servants of a higher duty of accountability to the Singapore public, not just to Ministers and the Government.

sections.label: Support for clause 6 information sharing
sections.summary: The passage supports clause 6, which grants authority for public sector bodies to share information for greater expediency and efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Like many others in this House, I support clause 6 that makes provisions and grants authority for public sector bodies to share information.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is necessary to allow greater expediency and efficiency for data and information to be shared among different public sector bodies to help Singaporeans, be it in healthcare, education, housing, retirement adequacy or social and financial support.

sections.label: Support for clauses 7, 15, 16
sections.summary: The passage supports clause 7 on confidentiality and privacy conditions, and clauses 15 and 16 on CE appointments approved by the Minister with PSC concurrence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, it is understandable that there is a concern with the confidentiality and privacy of such information sharing with self-help organisations or public sector institutions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I support clause 7 that sets out the conditions and extent of the proposed law that would protect the confidentiality, privacy and use of such information.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The other concern I have is in clauses 15 and 16.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I support that the appointment of the CE of a public sector agency is to be approved by the Minister, with the concurrence of PSC.

sections.label: Support for Bill and Statutory Board amendments
sections.summary: The passage compares the practice to the private sector and supports the Bill, noting amendments mainly streamline and standardise corporate governance provisions across Statutory Boards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Similar practices are carried out in the private sector where the decisions to employ or dismiss senior executives of a company are made in consultation with the board of directors or advisors of the company.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the concerns I have raised, I support this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is notable that the amendments are mainly for the purpose of streamlining and standardising the corporate governance provision across the various Statutory Boards.

sections.label: Data protection and sharing safeguards
sections.summary: The passage states data must be protected from misuse, with clear guidelines on shareable data and a mechanism with safeguards for public-private data sharing.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is important to protect these data as they can be subjected to misuse.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There should be clear guidelines on which data can be shared and which data cannot be shared among public sector institutions, for instance, in healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There should also be a mechanism in place with adequate safeguards where the public sector and private sector are able to share relevant data to benefit Singaporeans and Singapore as a whole.

sections.label: Strategic resource plan for Budget
sections.summary: A strategic resource plan should accompany the Annual Budget to deter unreasonable and excessive spending.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, there should be a strategic resource plan accompanying the Annual Budget to deter unreasonable and excessive spending.

sections.label: Covered walkways near MRT stations
sections.summary: LTA has put up covered walkways within 400 metres of MRT stations, covering exits to surrounding pathways.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Certainly, there is more than a single approach or solution to every challenge, and not trying but leaving things to the status quo will make us worse off in the long run.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I am sure many have heard that to enable a better first- and last-mile connectivity, LTA has put up covered walkways within 400 metres of Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) stations.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: By default, the walkways will cover the different exits of each MRT station to the immediate surrounding pathways.

sections.label: Neighbours for Active Living befriending
sections.summary: Under the South-East CDC, volunteers were matched as befrienders with vulnerable elderly, reducing their hospital admission rate.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: However, with the advent of technology, more data are generated from the sources we interact with on a daily basis.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: And as reflected in some of the initiatives in collaboration with the Ministries, data has shown to effectively assist the individuals, especially the vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Take, for example, under the South-East Community Development Council (CDC), the programme that is called "Neighbours for Active Living", volunteers have been successfully matched as befrienders with vulnerable elderly who are living on their own, those who are also frequent admitters to hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The regular visits by the volunteers have reduced the admission rate of those vulnerable elderly and certainly given them friends who became their friend and their "family".

sections.label: Privacy and personal choice under PDPA
sections.summary: Changes enabling collaboration must respect individuals' privacy and wishes and be built on personal choice as set out in PDPA.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: With this said, I do recognise that individuals’ privacy and wishes must still be respected and honoured.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Thus, any changes to enable the inter-agencies, voluntary groups and individuals and the community to collaborate must be built upon the fundamental principle of personal choice as set out in PDPA.

sections.label: Wider public consultation on Bills
sections.summary: More Bills with societal or family impact should get wider public consultation, with more time for views online, offline and in person.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Second, allow more Bills with societal impact or related to family to a wider public consultation process.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Provide more time for the public to provide objective, constructive views both online and offline and in in-person sessions to seek views extensively and have more thorough discussions before the Bills are passed.

sections.label: Corporate governance for Statutory Boards
sections.summary: Given recent impropriety at Government-linked companies like Keppel, the Bill reinforces corporate governance processes across all Statutory Boards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given the recent unfortunate incidents of impropriety amongst Government-linked companies, such as Keppel, this Bill provides a most timely reinforcement and strengthening of corporate governance processes across all Statutory Boards.

sections.label: CEO stint length concerns
sections.summary: A Civil Service career may stretch leaders across sectors, but a two- or three-year stint may not let a CEO understand the industry or build culture and governance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From a Civil Service career perspective, this may be intended to expose and stretch these leaders in a variety of sectors and experiences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, there is concern that in some sectors, a two- or three-year stint might not provide enough time for a CEO to fully understand the industry and to build a strong corporate culture and governance ethos.

sections.label: SMRT CEO culture issues
sections.summary: The CEO of Singapore Mass Rapid Transit is still grappling with internal culture issues after five years on the job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we were informed late last year, the CEO of Singapore Mass Rapid Transit is still grappling with internal culture issues, this, after five years on the job!

sections.label: Transparency over leadership appointments
sections.summary: Perhaps more transparency over Board and leadership appointments, and leadership performance, is warranted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Perhaps a little more transparency over Board and leadership appointments, as well as leadership performance, is warranted.

sections.label: Bill scope excludes Public Service
sections.summary: Most clauses apply to the Singapore Public Sector Agency, a term excluding the Public Service, which includes SAF, SCDF, Civil Service, Legal Service and SPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The bulk of the clauses in the Bill apply to the "Singapore Public Sector Agency", the term excludes the "Public Service", defined to include SAF, SCDF, Singapore Civil Service, Singapore Legal Service and Singapore Police Force (SPF), effectively limiting much of the scope of the Bill to cover only "Public Bodies" and "Singapore Public Sector Agencies".

sections.label: Clarify Public Service exclusion
sections.summary: The Minister is asked why the Public Service is excluded from most clauses though those entities deliver services to the public, and how the Bill's objectives will be fulfilled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify why the Public Service is excluded from the bulk of these clauses, especially since I understand that the aforementioned entities defined as Public Service in the Bill also delivers services to the public?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given the objective of the Bill is to better establish a consistent system of governance and accountability, can the Minister clarify how these objectives will be fulfilled when important agencies, such as SAF, SCDF, the Singapore Civil Service, the Singapore Legal Service and SPF are excluded?

sections.label: Clarify five agencies' exclusion
sections.summary: The Minister is asked how the five agencies defined as Public Service differ from Public Bodies, given the Bill's aim to break down silos and standardise governance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, Deputy Prime Minister Teo mentioned recently at the Public Service Leadership Dinner on 8 November last year, I quote, "the challenges that confront Singapore and Singaporeans often cannot be compartmentalised." Keeping in mind the objective of the Bill, which is to break down intra- and interagency silos to enable a consistent system of governance, can the Minister clarify specifically how different these five agencies are defined as Public Service as compared to Public Bodies such that standard governance rules as envisioned in the Bill should not apply equally across the board?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Even though most of our data have gone digital, our vision for whole-of-Government coordination to provide a unified platform of services has only been partially realised.

sections.label: Consolidating government data and information
sections.summary: It argues for consolidating government-related data to avoid duplication, reduce red tape, boost efficiency and enhance coordination of planning and services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding, since we view Government-related services and transactions as a whole, it is better to consolidate data and information to avoid duplication, reduce red tape, boost efficiency and enhance coordination of planning and services.

sections.label: Private doctors sharing patient records
sections.summary: It asks about progress in getting private medical practitioners to share consolidated patient records with MOH, and cites a study on IT professionals accessing information they were not permitted to access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, what is the progress in getting private medical practitioners to share their consolidated patient records with the Ministry of Health (MOH), which is necessary for better health care management of patients?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A recent study found that nearly half of IT professionals have sought information they were not permitted to access.

sections.label: Minister answerable for Statutory Board
sections.summary: It states the responsible Minister is answerable to Parliament for the Statutory Board's performance, and that direction and CE appointment powers align with this accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The responsible Minister is answerable to Parliament for the performance of the Statutory Board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The powers to give directions to the Statutory Board and to approve the appointment of the CE are in line with this accountability to Parliament.

sections.label: Stocktake of Statutory Board Acts
sections.summary: It states central agencies did a stocktake of all Statutory Board Acts and found not all important governance provisions were uniformly present across all Acts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The central agencies, therefore, did a stocktake of all the Statutory Board Acts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And they found that, of the governance provisions that are important to uphold to sustain good governance, not all were uniformly present across all Acts.

sections.label: CE collaboration with public agencies
sections.summary: It states that it is being made explicit that part of the CE of a Statutory Board's work is to collaborate with other public agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: One, is that we are making it explicit that part of the work of the CE of a Statutory Board is to collaborate with other public agencies.

sections.label: Directions and CE cooperation duties
sections.summary: It states the Bill clarifies how the public sector Minister can work with relevant Ministers to give directions to Statutory Boards on central policies, and that CEs must cooperate and collaborate with other public sector agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For example, the Bill clarifies how the Minister charged with the responsibility for the public sector can work with the relevant Ministers to give directions to Statutory Boards relating to central policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And that, second, the CEs of Statutory Boards now, by law, have to cooperate and collaborate with other public sector agencies to deliver public value.

sections.label: Statutory Boards and public sector scope
sections.summary: Clause 4 gives legislative backing to Statutory Boards' compliance, and the Bill applies broadly to Singapore public sector agencies including Ministries, Statutory Boards and Organs of State.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Statutory Boards are already complying with the Government's central policies today, and clause 4 gives this legislative backing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Simply put, the Bill is written such that the provisions apply by and large to the Singapore public sector agencies, and the Singapore public sector agencies is broadly defined to include Ministries and departments, Statutory Boards and Organs of State.

sections.label: Notice of Amendment and PA exemption
sections.summary: The effect of the Notice of Amendment will be that PA is not exempted from it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The answer is that the effect of the Notice of Amendment will be that PA is not exempted from it.

sections.label: Minister's direction and written law
sections.summary: The Minister's direction cannot be inconsistent with written law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: First, the Minister's direction cannot be inconsistent with written law.

sections.label: Minister's direction and independent functions
sections.summary: The Minister's direction cannot impede or affect the performance of statutorily independent or quasi-judicial functions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Second, the Minister's direction cannot impede or affect the performance of statutorily independent or quasi-judicial functions.

sections.label: Ministerial direction on specific employees
sections.summary: Clause 11(3)(b) prohibits Ministerial directions specific to a case, such as securing employment, promotion or termination of a particular public sector employee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The third area of safeguard is that the Minister’s direction should not be specific to a case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, clause 11(3)(b) prohibits any Ministerial direction to secure an employment, a promotion or a termination of any particular employee of a Singapore public sector agency.

sections.label: Data-sharing directive and public purposes
sections.summary: The data-sharing directive strengthens cross-agency data-sharing rules, and the Bill provides bases for sharing data for seven specific public purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The data-sharing directive seeks to strengthen the rules that enable and govern cross-agency data-sharing within the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: First, the Bill provides the bases for data to be shared and there are seven specific public purposes, as stated in the Bill.

sections.label: Data-sharing for policy analysis
sections.summary: A second benefit of data-sharing is better policy analysis, planning and formulation, involving anonymised, non-identifiable data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The second benefit for data-sharing is better policy analysis, planning and formulation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This will involve sharing of anonymised, non-identifiable data.

sections.label: Matching and anonymising raw data
sections.summary: Raw data from various agencies must come to a centre to be matched and anonymised before release to relevant agencies for analysis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: There is an immense amount of work we can do here to better understand the relation, say, between family backgrounds, education experiences, careers, employment, health, social security, so that we can formulate better policies to address our challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: However, to do so, raw data from various agencies need to come to a centre where they are matched and anonymised before release to relevant agencies for analysis.

sections.label: Four levels of protection
sections.summary: Beyond clear bases for data-sharing, there are four levels of protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Beyond the fact that there are now clear bases for data-sharing, there are four levels of protection.

sections.label: Legislated protection and criminal offences
sections.summary: Information protected by specific legislation continues to be protected, and criminal offences for three data-related offences are introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The third level is that information that is protected by specific legislation today, such as information under the Income Tax Act, the Banking Act and the Statistics Act, will continue to be protected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Four, criminal offences for three data-related offences are also introduced in the Bill to ensure individual officers are responsible and accountable for safeguarding information.

sections.label: Sharing within the Public Service
sections.summary: The Bill covers only sharing of data within the Public Service, not beyond it to VWOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Miss Cheryl Chan asked about data-sharing beyond the Public Service, to VWOs, for example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This Bill covers only sharing of data within the Public Service.

sections.label: Verifying and updating personal data
sections.summary: Designated agencies will proactively verify and update specified personal data fields and share that across the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Accuracy of a citizen's personal data is critical for seamless service delivery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We will assign designated agencies to proactively verify and update specified personal data fields and share that across the Government, so that all agencies’ databases are up to date and accurate.

sections.label: Sensitive data in designated databases
sections.summary: More sensitive information such as identifiable data will be held in designated databases with more limited access and additional protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: More sensitive information, such as identifiable data, will be held in designated databases with even more limited access and additional protection.

sections.label: Unauthorised access criminalised under CMCA
sections.summary: Deliberate unauthorised access of information is criminalised under other legislation such as the Computer Misuse and Cybersecurity Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Deliberate unauthorised access of information is criminalised under other legislation, such as the Computer Misuse and Cybersecurity Act (CMCA).

sections.label: Cybersecurity capabilities and CSA
sections.summary: The Cyber Security Agency, established 1 April 2015, oversees national cybersecurity strategy, and from mid-2017 Government network devices could not access the Internet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Second, is to institutionalise our cybersecurity capabilities and that is done through the Cyber Security Agency (CSA), established on 1 April 2015, to oversee a new national cybersecurity structure, with the mandate to devise and coordinate national cybersecurity strategy and policy development, carry out both peacetime capability development and crisis management across all sectors and, finally, adopt a holistic approach towards the management of information infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In May 2016, the Singapore Government decided that devices connected to Government networks would no longer be able to access the Internet, in order to strengthen the Government's information and communications technology systems and this was implemented in mid-2017.

sections.label: PA Governing Board appointing CE
sections.summary: The amendments give the PA Governing Board power to appoint the Association's CE with the Minister's approval and PSC's concurrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move the amendments* (1) to (4) standing in my name, as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This amendments will mean that the Governing Board of PA will have the power to appoint the Association’s CE, with the approval of the responsible Minister and the concurrence of PSC, as is the case for similar Statutory Boards.

sections.label: Removal of PA CE
sections.summary: The amendments mean the PA CE must not be removed from office without the Minister's approval and PSC's concurrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move the amendments* (1) and (2) standing in my name, as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: These amendments mean that the CE of PA must not be removed from that office without the approval of the Minister and the concurrence of PSC, as is the case for similar Statutory Boards.

sections.label: Recovering funds from volunteers
sections.summary: The amendment allows the Government to recover funds from any volunteer who mismanages the public moneys they are given responsibility for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But such volunteers do handle public monies from time to time, and, as best as we try to prevent it, there are sometimes instances in which volunteers mismanage these monies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This amendment will allow the Government to recover funds from any volunteer who mismanages the public moneys they are given responsibility for.
